arc.scene1_hook: Open on a glowing compass needle spinning inside a person's chest silhouette. The needle settles — pointing toward a gold trophy icon. The silhouette glows with confidence. But then we pull back: dozens of identical silhouettes, all with compasses, all pointing the exact same direction. The "inner drive" is suspiciously uniform. Title pill: "YOUR DREAMS WERE NEVER YOURS".
arc.scene2_mystery: A child silhouette sits at center frame building a block tower — pure, pre-rational desire. Around her, faint outlines of adults (parent, teacher, screen) radiate lines toward her like signal towers. The compass needle inside her chest slowly rotates to match. Below, a timeline bar shows ages 0→5→10→15, and with each tick, the child's tower morphs: first it's freeform blocks, then a diploma shape, then a dollar sign shape. The "inner ambition" is being sculpted in real time by external signals she can't see.
arc.scene3_wrong_answer: The obvious assumption: your goals come from within. A brain icon pulses at center with radiating light — "INNER DRIVE" label. Arrows point outward from brain to targets (career, money, status). It looks like the brain is the origin. Clean, heroic, self-made. A confidence meter fills to 100%. The visual sells the myth of autonomous desire — that ambition wells up from some authentic core self.
arc.scene4_contradiction: The brain visual cracks. We reverse the arrows — now they point INWARD. A TV screen icon, a parent silhouette, a social media phone icon, a school building — all firing signals INTO the brain. The "INNER DRIVE" label glitches and rewrites to "INSTALLED DRIVE". The compass needle that seemed so personal? Zoom out to show it was magnetized by someone else's field all along. A doctor-family silhouette has a compass pointing to a stethoscope. A hustle-culture phone screen has compasses pointing to dollar signs. The metrics chose them.
arc.scene5_proof: Three parallel columns showing the installation mechanism. Column 1: doctor-family → child compass → stethoscope (labeled "MEDICINE"). Column 2: hustle-media → child compass → revenue chart (labeled "REVENUE"). Column 3: social-screen → child compass → eye/visibility icon (labeled "VISIBILITY"). Below each, a counter: "CHOSE THIS? NO" in red. At the bottom, a quote-style label: "The metrics were already in the room when they arrived." The evidence is structural — none of these people selected their metrics from a neutral catalog.
arc.scene6_betrayal: Return to the original confident silhouette from Scene 1. But now the compass in its chest is visibly connected by thin red threads to external sources — media towers, family figures, institutional buildings. The silhouette reaches for its compass to "follow its heart" — but the threads pull taut. The glow fades. What felt like inner fire was an echo. The final image: the silhouette stands among hundreds of identical ones, all connected, all "following their hearts" in the same direction. A small child silhouette at the bottom still builds a freeform tower — the only one not connected.

tts_script: You learn what success is long before you learn to question it. It arrives in childhood like a compass needle, pointing somewhere you haven't been yet but are certain exists. But look closer, and the compass starts to wobble. What you thought was inner orientation turns out to be an echo. Your ambition maps suspiciously well onto the ambitions of the people around you, the images you consumed, the stories you were told. The child in a family of doctors learns medicine is the tall tower. The child scrolling curated lives learns visibility is arrival. None of them chose their metrics. The metrics were already in the room when they arrived. The first crack in success is the recognition that the compass was magnetized by someone else's field.
